root_draft.speaker: agent
root_draft.text: FeverWood makes a home in the treetops depend on respecting the black water below. Living wood carries the colony's roads and growing ground; the marsh refuses heavy buildings unless the colony invests in stilts. The pools are openings onto one vast sekkulaath: its different tentacles threaten, watch and lay out treasure, and what happens at the water has lasting consequences. The colony learns when to approach, when to rescue someone, and when to fight for respite or a lasting victory over its own pools. Above them, alien animals make a living crown, and keeping the nectar herd calm matters to the colony's livelihood. Living bait can draw two enemies into a staggered fight; the kurreth hive offers a separate expedition into an enemy that notices intrusion and closes the way back. Imprisoning the deep's young buys useful products and risks an escape; returning them buys a gift. On hot days, doubled oil harvest tempts workers into haze that a spark can ignite. Ordinary play shows the creature through its limbs; the whole body's rising belongs to the campaign's separate plot.

experience_source.text: A world in the treetops above a black mirror nobody touches. You live on the branches, and the water remembers.
